Definition: from G1492; a view, i.e. form (literally or figuratively):--appearance, fashion, shape, sight.
BiblicalUsage: This word is a form or appearance, what a thing looks like when you see it, and the New Testament uses it for the deepest sights. At Jesus' baptism the Holy Spirit descends in bodily shape like a dove, on the mountain His face changes and His clothing becomes white and glistering, and the Father says no one has seen His form or heard His voice at any time. Paul closes his letter by telling the Thessalonians to abstain from all appearance of evil, because what a thing looks like matters too.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the form matters because God showed Himself in one, and the Spirit came down where everyone could see. I hold that we should avoid even the appearance of evil, because the look of a thing teaches before its words do.
RelatedTopics: Outpouring of the Spirit; Jesus Christ; Holiness
